subagent_reports.topic: Two-layer split validation: structural membership + heuristic ranking hint for prioritized work queue

sources.label: YouTube DNN two-stage recommender (Google Research)
sources.summary: Canonical two-stage architecture: candidate generation (high recall, broad) then ranking (high precision, fine scoring). Explicitly states the two-stage split lets you recommend from a huge corpus while keeping the surfaced set personalized \u2014 i.e. eligibility and ordering are intentionally separate concerns.

sources.label: Pinterest multi-stage retrieval+ranking
sources.summary: Confirms industry-standard funnel: retrieval narrows billions\u2192thousands, ranking scores the trimmed set. Retrieval intentionally over-inclusive (recall); ranking does discrimination (precision). Collapsing retrieval into a precision classifier loses recall.

sources.label: GitHub Issue Types docs (GA Jan 2025)
sources.summary: Issue Types are OPTIONAL metadata. Defaults task/bug/feature shipped per org. Phrasing 'when you add an issue type to an issue' confirms not required. Evolved from labels; an issue can have no type.

sources.label: GitHub Issues about (types as metadata)
sources.summary: Lists 'issue types, labels and milestones' together as organizational metadata \u2014 none required-to-create.

sources.label: Jira default issue type (per-project scheme)
sources.summary: Jira issue type IS required at creation and solved via a per-project default in the issue-type scheme. Confirms the required-field model needs a default to avoid blocking creation.

sources.label: Jira required-field creation block (failure mode)
sources.summary: Documents the failure mode of required-without-default: users blocked from creating issues with ': is required' error until a value/default is supplied. Concrete evidence of required-enum friction.

sources.label: Linear Triage docs
sources.summary: Linear has NO first-class issue-type field; uses labels+priority+status. Triage is an inbox. Enforcement is opt-in at triage EXIT ('Can I require priority before an issue leaves Triage? Yes'), not at creation \u2014 the advisory\u2192enforcement graduation pattern.

sources.label: GitLab Issue Type design blueprint
sources.summary: GitLab explicitly deprecated 'Issue Types' in favor of Work Items / Work Item Types; issue-type-as-extension was rejected as a model. Heavyweight type systems were moved away from.

sources.label: Conventional Commits 1.0.0 spec
sources.summary: Spec authors acknowledge imperfect conformance: 'In a worst case scenario, it's not the end of the world if a commit lands that does not meet the spec. It simply means that commit will be missed by tools.' Types beyond feat/fix allowed, casing flexible \u2192 prefix is a recognized but LOSSY signal. Supports hint-not-gate use.

sources.label: Expand-contract migration pattern (Prisma)
sources.summary: Canonical safe schema migration: add nullable/default enum first (expand), backfill, then constrain (contract). Adding NOT NULL enum with no default to existing rows is the documented failure path.

sources.label: PostgreSQL add-column-backfill expand-contract
sources.summary: 'ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL in one statement fails as soon as the table contains rows.' Confirms required-with-backfill is a real migration hazard; optional-with-default sidesteps it.

sources.label: Alarm fatigue scoping review (BMC Nursing)
sources.summary: Honest counter-case: excessive/false alarms cause desensitization, delayed response, deactivation. Applies to ACTION-DEMANDING heuristic signals; mitigated when signal is passive reordering with visible confidence.

sources.label: Developer trust erosion in AppSec
sources.summary: False-positive rates 30-70% erode trust; engineers abandon tools when investigation cost > perceived benefit. Counter-case evidence for noisy heuristic labels; supports making evidence/confidence visible (which the advisory label does).

sources.label: ADV codebase established invariant (adv-coordinate.md / adv-triage.md)
sources.summary: Codebase ALREADY mandates: 'Epic membership remains optional; order stays advisory \u2014 may guide display/next-work but must not block gates, tasks, promotion, or change progress.' Ranking uses existing signals (issue priority, gate proximity, recency) and is explicitly never a filter/authorizer. The proposed change is consistent with this proven invariant; the rejected structural-enum alternative would DEPART from it.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The two-layer split (structural eligibility + heuristic advisory ranking) is the canonical multi-stage funnel pattern documented at industrial scale by YouTube and Pinterest: retrieval/eligibility is intentionally high-recall and over-inclusive, ranking is high-precision discrimination. Collapsing eligibility into a precision classifier (i.e. letting a defect/feature classifier gate visibility) is exactly the anti-pattern the recsys literature warns against. Locally, the ADV codebase already encodes this exact invariant for Epic ordering ('order stays advisory \u2014 may guide display/next-work but must not block gates, tasks, promotion, or change progress'), and the existing triage ranking already uses advisory existing-signals (issue priority, gate proximity, recency) with explicit non-filtering. The proposed change (title prefix + existing origin.kind provenance enum, advisory label, never filters/suppresses/authorizes) is fully consistent with the codebase's proven pattern and reuses an already-declared structural field (origin.kind) rather than minting a new one \u2014 a P19/P38 win (declaration that already has runtime effect, vs a freshly-inferred title prefix). The rejected structural change_kind enum is heavier, carries documented backfill/required-field friction (Jira-style), and would diverge from the codebase's own established non-blocking advisory invariant. Mature trackers split cleanly: GitHub (optional types, GA 2025) and Linear (no type field, opt-in enforcement at triage exit) chose the advisory/optional model; only Jira uses required-issue-type, and it pays for it with documented creation-blocking failure modes.

validation.notes: All five sub-questions resolve to Confirmed or Caution; none to Conflict. No blockers. The chosen approach matches both external canonical practice and the codebase's own established invariant. Counter-case (Q4) is honestly engaged and is mitigated by the proposal's own design (advisory label, never filters/authorizes) plus a recommended graduation path (optional now, opt-in enforcement at triage-exit later if signal proves trustworthy \u2014 Linear's model).

tradeoffs: Two-layer means ranking quality is bounded by hint signal quality (title prefix is lossy; origin.kind is stronger). If hints mislabel, ordering is suboptimal but never wrong about what EXISTS \u2014 acceptable failure mode.
Advisory hints can be devalued/ignored if consistently noisy (trust erosion, Q4). Mitigated by visible advisory label + reusing the structural origin.kind signal as the primary hint.

Rejecting structural change_kind foregoes future queryability/aggregation by defect-vs-feature (e.g. 'bug backlog burn-down'). Recoverable later via optional field + expand-contract if a real need emerges; YAGNI today.
Required-field model (Jira-style) trades stronger guarantees for creation friction and one-time backfill risk over ~50 existing items; not justified by current advisory-only use.

alternatives_considered.option: Structural change_kind enum, required at creation + backfill ~50 items (rejected alternative)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Heavier, documented backfill/required-field friction (Jira ': is required' block; expand-contract needed), diverges from codebase's established non-blocking advisory invariant, and YAGNI for an advisory-only ranking use. Reconsider ONLY if a downstream consumer needs defect-vs-feature as a hard query dimension; then add optional-with-default and graduate, not required-from-day-one.
Loses signal that defect/bugfix work often wants to surface ahead of feature work in a 'what next' queue. Advisory hint is cheap and reversible; pure label gives no ordering input.

alternatives_considered.option: Heuristic as a hard filter (classifier gates visibility)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Anti-pattern per recsys two-stage literature: collapsing high-recall eligibility into a precision classifier loses recall and mis-hides eligible work when the classifier is wrong (which CC-prefix on free-text titles frequently is).

alternatives_considered.option: Advisory now, opt-in enforcement at triage-exit later (Linear model)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Not a replacement for the chosen approach \u2014 a sequenced evolution framing. Start advisory (this change); if the hint signal proves trustworthy over time, allow opt-in 'require kind before leaving triage' later. Matches Linear's documented pattern and keeps the barrier-to-entry low now.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed with the two-layer split as proposed. Concrete refinements: (1) Treat origin.kind (already-declared structural provenance) as the PRIMARY ranking hint and title-prefix 'fix*' as a SECONDARY/weak hint \u2014 origin.kind has runtime effect today, the prefix does not (P38). # Broaden coordinate and triage coverage

## Intent

Make `/adv-coordinate` analyze every open/in-progress change in the project regardless of Epic linkage, and make `/adv-triage` surface fixes and defects tracked in ADV changes — not only GitHub issues.

## Origin

**Non-defect.** Both are desired new behavior stated by the user ("coordinate should consider all changes", "triage should include fixes and defects noted in advance changes"). Neither command promises this behavior today, so no Root Cause Analysis obligation attaches under rq-defectOriginRca01.

## Current-state evidence

### Coordinate: listed but not analyzed

`rq-epicCoordinateProjectInventory01.1` already requires inventorying every participating project's in-flight changes with complete pagination. That part lands. Every *analytic* phase, however, keys off Epic entries:

| Phase | Operates on |
|---|---|
| 3 Repo overlap | "Shell entries" and "Linked changes" only |
| 4 Alignment | Epic dimensions (ownership, narrative, cross-Epic deps) |
| 5 Sequencing | entry success hints, terminal summaries |
| 6 Membership health | Epic projection state |
| 6.5 Refactor coverage | all nonterminal changes, Epic-linked or not — but reachable only past Phase 1 |

Phase 6.5 explicitly declares its candidate population as "every nonterminal in-flight change from the Phase 1 project inventory, whether or not it is linked to an Epic", then negates that reach with: "runs only when coordination proceeds past Phase 1. When Phase 1 short-circuits on no active Epics, the audit does not run."

Consequence: an unlinked open change is listed and never analyzed. A project with zero Epics receives an inventory and no drift analysis, despite Phase 6.5 requiring no Epic input.

Measured in this repo at contract time: 50 in-flight changes, 4 carrying `epic_membership`. 46 of 50 fall into "listed, not analyzed".

### Triage: changes are a matching corpus, not a defect source

- Phase 2 lists "active ADV changes" as a source, but Phase 3 consumes them only to decide whether a GitHub *issue* is `represented[]`.
- Phase 4c bug priority loop is `gh issue edit --add-label` — GitHub-only by construction. The constraint "MUST NOT write `priority:*` labels to non-bug issues" confirms the label surface is issue-scoped. No path assigns priority to a change.
- Phase 6 *Open issues worth solving* is defined as "open issues with no linked active ADV change" — issues-only by definition.
- Phase 6 *Important to complete* ranks by linked issue priority first. A defect change with no GitHub issue ranks `none` and sorts below feature work carrying a `priority:low` issue.
- `kind_hint` exists in the Phase 2 inventory record, is marked advisory, and feeds no downstream decision.

Measured in this repo at contract time: 24 of 50 in-flight changes are `fix*`-prefixed, none showing issue linkage in list output.

## LBP targets

1. **Coordinate de-gating.** Detach Phase 6.5 reachability from the no-active-Epics short-circuit; extend Phase 3 and Phase 5 coverage to unlinked changes. Must not violate the existing command boundary: no task creation, no gate completion, no Epic auto-enrollment, Epic order stays advisory.
2. **Triage change representation.** Decide whether defect-shaped ADV changes receive a priority signal or only a render slot. `priority:*` is a GitHub label surface; changes have no label surface. A parallel priority mechanism for changes is a durable design decision, not a rendering tweak.
3. **Boundary preservation.** `/adv-cleanup` retains change closure. `/adv-coordinate` retains Epic repair. `/adv-triage` retains issue linkage. Neither expansion may absorb a neighbor's authority.
4. **`kind_hint` disposition.** Currently advisory and unconsumed. Decide whether it becomes structural (P33) or remains discovery-only. If defect classification drives ranking, heuristic title prefixes such as `fix*` must not become the sole authority.
5. **Existing projection reuse.** Both commands already consume `adv_resume_projection`. Determine whether `ordered_next` / `actionable[]` already supplies Epic-independent change ordering before building a new ranking mechanism.

## Scope

- `.opencode/command/adv-coordinate.md` — Phases 3, 5, 6.5, 7
- `.opencode/command/adv-triage.md` — Phases 2, 6
- `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json` — neighbors of `rq-epicCoordinateProjectInventory01`
- triage-owning spec capability — to be resolved during discovery
- `skills/adv-triage/SKILL.md`
- `plugin/src/advance-epics-assets.test.ts` plus the triage asset test
- deployed mirrors under `~/.config/opencode/command/`

## User outcomes

- `/adv-coordinate` in a zero-Epic project returns drift findings, not just an inventory.
- An unlinked open change receives the same overlap and sequencing scrutiny as an Epic-linked one.
- `/adv-triage` "what should I work on" surfaces defect work tracked only in ADV.
- Defect changes stop ranking below feature work whose only advantage is a linked `priority:low` issue.

## Retracted finding: adv_change_list pagination

An earlier reading of this session claimed `adv_change_list` silently truncates at 50 rows. **That claim is retracted as incorrect.**

Original observation: `limit: 200` returned 50 rows with `pagination.total: 50, hasMore: false`, while `hydrationStats.totalIds` read 158.

Re-verification after the in-flight population grew to 51:

| Call | `total` | `returned` | `hasMore` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit: 5` | 51 | 5 | true, with `resumeHint` |
| `limit: 200, offset: 50` | 51 | 1 | false |

`pagination.total` reports population size, not returned count. A per-page cap of 50 exists, but `hasMore` and `resumeHint` signal continuation correctly, and `offset: 50` correctly returns the 51st row.

Two errors produced the false finding:

1. The in-flight population was *exactly* 50 at observation time, so `total: 50, hasMore: false` was accurate. A coincidence was read as a cap.
2. `hydrationStats.totalIds: 158` counts all changes including archived and closed — a different population from in-flight. Comparing it against the in-flight count violated P39 (population identity): numerator and denominator were not drawn from the same verified population.

No pagination defect exists. No `/adv-problem` change is warranted. Coordinate's "complete pagination" requirement is satisfiable with the current tool, provided callers honor `hasMore` / `resumeHint` rather than assuming a single call returns the full set — which is itself worth asserting explicitly in the coordinate contract during design.

# Design — Broaden coordinate and triage coverage

> **Post-design corrections applied during execution.** Three claims in the original design and agreement were sourced from an `explore` sub-agent report and later disproved by direct inspection. They are corrected in place below and catalogued in the final section. Treat that section as authoritative where it conflicts with anything else.

## Root pattern

Three surfaces independently made Epic linkage a silent precondition for change visibility:

| Surface | Mechanism | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `/adv-coordinate` Phase 6.5 | reachability clause tied the audit to "coordination proceeds past Phase 1" | zero-Epic project got inventory, no drift analysis |
| `/adv-coordinate` Phases 3, 5 | analysis tables enumerated "Shell entries" and "Linked changes" only | unlinked change listed, never analyzed |
| `adv_resume_projection` | `computeChangeRank` returned `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` when `epic_membership` absent | one Epic-linked change permanently outranked every unlinked change |

`/adv-triage` had a fourth, related gap: `renderPortfolioBalance` sorted on `priorityWeight(linkedIssue?.priority)` first, so a change with no GitHub issue scored `0` and sank.

These are one defect shape — an optional organizing structure (Epic membership, issue linkage) silently acquiring gating authority over visibility. The repo's own invariant already forbids Epic order blocking *progress*; these surfaces gated *visibility*, which the invariant never covered.

## Decision 1 — Two-layer split for defect representation

No structural defect/fix classification exists on an ADV change. Verified absent: `origin.kind` is provenance not taxonomy; `capabilities[]` is subsystem tagging; `release_notes.category` carries a `fixed` value but is populated for almost no active change and is read only by the archive sidecar.

Rather than introduce a structural `change_kind` enum, the two concerns are separated:

| Concern | Mechanism | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Membership — which changes are eligible | structural: every nonterminal change with no linked issue | structural only; no heuristic decides eligibility |
| Ranking hint — which float up | heuristic: `origin.kind` primary, title prefix secondary | ordering only; never filters, suppresses, closes, or authorizes |

P33 permits exactly this: heuristics may assist discovery, ranking, and triage, but never own correctness, security, persistence, gate completion, or spec compliance. Ranking is sanctioned; selection is not.

Independent validation (adv-researcher, verdict `pass`, confidence high, risk low) confirmed this is the canonical two-stage retrieval/ranking funnel — deliberately over-inclusive candidate generation followed by discriminative ranking. Collapsing eligibility into a precision classifier is the named anti-pattern: it loses recall and hides work when the classifier is wrong.

Tracker prior art supports optional-and-advisory over required-and-structural: GitHub Issue Types (GA 2025) are optional; Linear has no first-class type field and enforces priority only at triage *exit*; GitLab deprecated Issue Types in favour of Work Items. Jira alone requires type at creation, and compensates with a mandatory per-project default.

**Hint precedence.** `origin.kind` is primary because it is already wired and has runtime effect. Title prefix (`fix*`) is secondary and weak: Conventional Commits' own specification concedes non-conforming commits are simply "missed by tools", and ADV change titles are free text rather than CC-governed.

**Implemented weighting.** `PRIORITY_WEIGHT` rescaled to critical 40 / high 30 / medium 20 / low 10, with `DEFECT_HINT_WEIGHT = 15` placed strictly between `low` and `medium`. An advisory hint may lift defect work above the weakest structural triage signal but can never outrank a deliberate medium-or-higher human triage decision. Both boundary directions are pinned by tests.

**Placement.** Unlinked changes were folded into the existing *Important to complete* section rather than given a fourth section. Execution evidence drove this: the RED run showed membership tests already passing — `renderPortfolioBalance` never dropped unlinked rows. Membership was never the defect; ranking was. Folding fixes the real failure mode while preserving the "Emit exactly three sections" contract and the existing three-heading asset assertion.

### Rejected: structural `change_kind` enum

Deferred, not dismissed. Adding a required-ish enum to ~50 existing changes forces expand-contract migration or an `unknown` sentinel filtered everywhere, and diverges from the codebase's optional-and-advisory invariant. If a hard defect-vs-feature *query* dimension is later needed, add it optional-with-default and graduate enforcement Linear-style at triage exit.

## Decision 2 — Fix `computeChangeRank`, do not compensate around it

`adv_resume_projection` is consumed by both commands. Compensating at each command boundary would leave the shared kernel biased and duplicate the workaround (P40: repair the owning invariant).

**Implemented scheme.** `MAX_RANK` replaced by named `EPIC_BAND_SPAN` (10000) and `UNLINKED_ACTIVE_RANK` (9999). Unlinked changes rank from their own strongest available signal — `hasInProgressTasks`, the only intrinsic signal on `ChangeNodeInput`:

- in progress → `9999`, tail of the first Epic band: ahead of later-Epic work, never displacing the leading Epic band
- idle → `(epics.length + 1) * EPIC_BAND_SPAN`, finite and trailing

Epic-linked ranks are untouched, preserving relative Epic order and alignment with shell entries, which compute `epicIndex * 10000 + order` inline. Reachability-without-inversion is pinned by a dedicated regression test.

**Consequential behavior change.** Previously every unlinked change tied at `MAX_RANK`, so `ordered_next` resolved by array order. With the activity discriminator, in-progress unlinked work now wins. This surfaced as a genuine consumer regression at `src/tools/resume-projection.test.ts:245`, whose `ordered_next` expectation was incidental rather than intentional. It was updated with an explanatory comment; the test's real subject (bucket classification) is unchanged. The policy is now pinned explicitly by a kernel test rather than left incidental.

## Decision 3 — Spec-law home

`adv_resume_projection` had no spec coverage. Its defect is Epic-coupling law, so it homes in `advance-epics` alongside the coordinate requirements (P04 locality). Triage portfolio behaviour homes in `backlog-coordination`, which already owns `rq-backlogCoord05`/`07`/`09`.

| Capability | Requirement | Scenarios |
|---|---|---|
| `advance-epics` v1.14.0 | `rq-epicCoordinateChangeCoverage01` | .1-.4 |

| `backlog-coordination` v1.6.0 | `rq-backlogCoord10` | .1-.4 |

Placement is locality-driven: coordinate coverage neighbours the inventory requirement it extends; rank reachability neighbours the advisory-order requirement it preserves.

## Post-design corrections (authoritative)

Three claims originated in an `explore` sub-agent report and were propagated into the proposal, agreement, and task packets without independent verification. Direct inspection disproved all three. Recorded here so the acceptance review does not re-inherit them.

**1. `adv_change_list` does not silently truncate.** Retracted during the proposal phase. `pagination.total` reports population size; `hasMore` and `resumeHint` signal continuation correctly; `offset: 50` returns the 51st row. The original observation coincided with a population of exactly 50, and compared `hydrationStats.totalIds` (all changes, including archived and closed) against the in-flight count — a population mismatch under P39. No pagination defect exists. Callers must still honour `hasMore`/`resumeHint`, which `rq-epicCoordinateChangeCoverage01.4` now makes explicit.

**2. No locked assertion enforced the coordinate short-circuit ordering.** The design originally claimed `plugin/src/advance-epics-assets.test.ts:213-219` structurally enforced that the no-active-Epics short-circuit precedes the refactor-coverage audit. It does not. Those lines assert only that the string `No active Epics` appears *after* `adv_change_list` — that is `rq-epicCoordinateProjectInventory01.3` (inventory precedes the message), which this change deliberately preserves and which still passes, because the narrowed message retains the `No active Epics` prefix and Phase 1 still names `adv_change_list` first. **Consequence for AC8:** its first clause ("no longer enforces that the short-circuit precedes the refactor-coverage audit") is vacuous — that was never enforced. AC8's substantive obligation, asserting the new reachability contract, is real and unchanged.

By contrast, the claim about `plugin/src/projection/resume-projection.test.ts:270-288` was **accurate**: that test did exercise the MAX_RANK relationship. It still passes on its merits (Epic order 0 beats idle unlinked); only its stale `// no epic → MAX_RANK` comment needed correcting.

**3. `kind_hint` is not a declaration without a mechanism.** The design originally listed it alongside dead declarations (P38). It is not. `skills/adv-triage/SCHEMA.md` defines it on the inventory record for *any* source as `bug | feature | unknown`; `skills/adv-triage/PROMPTS.md` exposes `reclassify N as bug|feature` to flip it during Phase 4a approval; Phase 1 preflight guarantees the `bug`/`feature` labels exist; Phase 4a sets `ADV Type`; Phase 4c runs its priority loop over bugs. That is a real consumer chain.

`kind_hint` and `defectHint` are **distinct concepts**: `kind_hint` classifies a *source item being promoted to a GitHub issue*; `defectHint` ranks an *existing ADV change already tracked in ADV*. Acting on the incorrect premise, the delegated worker removed `kind_hint` from Phase 2, orphaning the reclassify prompt. # Executive Summary — Broaden coordinate triage coverage

## Outcome

Work that isn't filed under a big initiative is now visible and rankable again. Previously it could be silently pushed to the back of every list, and two planning commands went quiet in projects that had no initiatives at all.

## Why it matters

ADV lets you group related changes into an initiative, but grouping is meant to be optional. In practice it had stopped being optional.

- **Ungrouped work became unreachable.** The ranking function assigned every change without an initiative the worst possible score. Not "lower" — the maximum. So when ADV suggested what to work on next, ungrouped work could never be chosen, no matter how active or urgent it was. Since they all tied at the same worst score, ties were broken by list order, which is arbitrary.
- **Two commands went silent on projects with no initiatives.** The coordination command stopped after taking inventory and produced no analysis at all. For a project that had never created an initiative, it did nothing useful.
- **The portfolio view skipped changes with no linked issue.** They were being ranked into invisibility rather than excluded, which made it look like a filtering problem when it was actually an ordering problem.

## What was delivered

- **Ungrouped work is reachable again.** An active ungrouped change now ranks alongside the leading initiative rather than at the bottom. It can be suggested as next work when its own signals justify it — but it can never push aside the top of an initiative's queue. Both directions are locked down by tests.
- **Coordination works without initiatives.** Overlap, sequencing, and coverage analysis now run based on the changes themselves. A project with no initiatives gets real findings instead of an early stop.
- **Ungrouped and grouped work are analysed on equal terms**, carrying the same supporting evidence.
- **A defect hint that only affects ordering.** Changes that look like bug fixes can be nudged up the list. This is deliberately advisory: it is weighted below any deliberate human priority decision, so it can lift a bug above the weakest automatic signal but can never override a human judgement. Critically, it only reorders — it can never add, remove, hide, or filter anything, and a test enforces that the visible set is identical whether the hint is on or off.
- **Complete inventory.** The coordination command now explicitly reads through to the end of a paginated list rather than treating the first page as the whole picture.
- **Three new rules written into the project's spec law**, so this behaviour is now governed rather than incidental.

## Verification

- Static checks, type checks, schema, manifest, and formatting: clean, 0 errors.
- Targeted test suites: 131 of 131 passing, re-run after bringing the branch up to date with the main line.
- The ranking module gained its first test file — it previously had none.
- Independent review of the full change: no blocking findings, no changes required.
- Each behaviour change was written as a failing test first, then made to pass.

## Notable during development

Three claims made by automated helper agents were checked directly and found to be **wrong**, then corrected before they could cause damage:

- A claim that a list command was truncating results — it was not; the figures had been compared against mismatched populations.
- A claim that an existing test locked in the old behaviour — no such test existed. The belief had already spread into the design document and the work instructions before being caught.
- A claim that a configuration value was unused and safe to delete — it had a real consumer. It was deleted on that bad advice and then restored.

The pattern is worth noting: in each case a confident-sounding claim survived until someone read the actual code.

## Risks and follow-ups

- **Deployment required.** These are plugin and command changes. Nothing changes for a running system until this is merged, rebuilt, deployed, and the host restarted.
- **The new rules are recorded in the design document rather than as tracked spec deltas.** The rules themselves are written and verified; only the change-tracking trail is lighter than usual. The preceding change shipped the same way. Cosmetic, but it should be tidied up.
- **A structural way to classify change types was deliberately not built.** The defect hint is advisory only. A proper typed classification remains a future option, recorded and not started.
- **One thing to be aware of:** a repository hook copied this branch's command files into the live installation before the change was merged. The content is correct and about to ship anyway, but the hook should not deploy from an unmerged branch. Being redeployed from the main line after merge, and logged as a follow-up.
